milestone_brief:
### E13_S04b — Extend 256 KB byte cap to remaining tool handlers (closes Threat 4 partial-coverage gap)

**Status:** NEW (follow-up to E13_S04 + filed as `chris-dare-dev/arXMCP#1` by E13_S10 cumulative coverage audit)
**Tier:** 5
**Effort:** M
**Dependencies:** E13_S04 (cap helper already exists for `get_chunk` + `get_definitions`)

**Description.** E13_S04 (Threat 4 audit) shipped the 256 KB inline-content cap on tool results but only wired it into `get_chunk` and `get_definitions`. The E13_S10 cumulative threat-model coverage review surfaced this as the highest-priority real coverage gap (filed at `https://github.com/chris-dare-dev/arXMCP/issues/1`). This milestone extends the cap to every return-chunk-or-content tool that does not yet enforce it: `search_papers`, `find_equation`, `find_lemma_by_name`, `get_paper`, and `cite_neighbors`. The cap behavior must be identical to the existing pattern in `get_chunk` / `get_definitions` (256 KB inline budget; oversize content spills via `resource_link` per Threat 4's threat-model text in `.claude/notes/08-security-observability-ops.md`).

**Mitigation:** the existing cap helper / pattern (see `server/handlers/get_chunk.py` and `server/handlers/get_definitions.py` for the canonical implementations) is the contract; this milestone REUSES it across the missing handlers rather than re-implementing per-tool. If a shared helper does not yet exist, extract one as part of this work so the contract is single-sourced.

**Deliverables.**
- Patches to the five handler modules under `server/handlers/` (`search.py` / `equation.py` / `lemma.py` / `paper.py` / `citations.py` — exact filenames may differ; the implementer reads the actual layout) to enforce the cap.
- Extracted shared cap helper (if not already present) — single source of truth for the 256 KB threshold and the spillover envelope shape.
- Extension of `tests/security/test_resource_exhaustion.py` — new parametrized tests across all five newly-covered tools, exercising the over-cap rejection path. Existing `get_chunk` / `get_definitions` tests stay as regression guards.
- Update `.claude/docs/security-threat-model-coverage.md` Threat 4 row: replace the `[#1 — extend 256 KB byte cap to remaining tool handlers](URL)` gap link with `(none)`; add a note in the body section that the gap is closed by this milestone. Update the Gap-issue triage table to mark G1 as closed.
- Close `chris-dare-dev/arXMCP#1` via `gh issue close` once the implementation lands (Phase 4 external-write boundary).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [ ] Every return-chunk-or-content tool (`get_chunk`, `get_definitions`, `search_papers`, `find_equation`, `find_lemma_by_name`, `get_paper`, `cite_neighbors`) enforces the 256 KB cap with identical semantics.
- [ ] `tests/security/test_resource_exhaustion.py` includes parametrized cap-rejection tests for all five newly-covered tools.
- [ ] `pytest tests/security/test_resource_exhaustion.py` passes all cases (existing + new).
- [ ] `.claude/docs/security-threat-model-coverage.md` Threat 4 row no longer cites #1; Gap-issue triage table updated.
- [ ] `tests/security/test_threat_model_coverage.py` (E13_S10 staleness gate) still passes (the doc edit must keep the per-threat structure intact).
- [ ] GitHub issue #1 closed with a commit reference.

**Out of scope.** Adding NEW resource caps beyond the 256 KB inline budget (e.g. per-call rate-limiting refinements). Extending the cap to non-tool surfaces (logs, metrics, health endpoints). Refactoring the cap value itself.

**Risk notes.**
- Closes G1 (MEDIUM) from `.claude/docs/security-threat-model-coverage.md` E13_S10 gap-issue triage.
- The cap helper extraction is mildly invasive (touches 5+ handler files); a focused critic pass should verify no handler-specific edge case is broken (e.g. `get_paper` may return metadata-only results that have always been under the cap by construction — the cap check must be defensive but not break the happy path).

**Labels.** `area:security`, `area:server`, `risk:medium`, `tier:5`, `closes:#1`
